editorial_note: Evidence is sourced. Interpretations and proposed tests are research notes developed with AI assistance, not company roadmaps.

ideas.title: A Moore’s law for brain interfaces?
ideas.question: Are we doubling electrodes, recording channels, or useful information?
ideas.summary: The apparent doubling rate changes with the thing being counted. Follow the same hardware from physical sites to simultaneous signals.
ideas.observation: A lab can move from a few probes to thousands of channels. The counting unit often changes along the way: thread, array, assembled implant, or acquisition system.
ideas.interpretation: The Neuropixels 2017-to-2025 site comparison gives an endpoint-equivalent doubling time of 2.99 years. Its simultaneous channels remain 384. That supports a specific site-count observation, not a universal three-year law.
ideas.test: Build separate dated series for the same interface, species, implant duration, and denominator. Compare sites per probe, concurrent channels per subject, and usable channels at a fixed implant age.
ideas.revision: Initial evidence review. A universal three-year doubling cadence and the exact local lab history remain unverified.

history.change: Initial evidence review. A universal three-year doubling cadence and the exact local lab history remain unverified.

ideas.title: Where should the next electrode go?
ideas.question: Does sampling more densely beat sampling a larger region?
ideas.summary: Adding contacts to one array and adding another array are different experiments. The value of the next contact may depend more on location than on the total.
ideas.observation: Precision’s four-array demonstration increased covered surface area. BrainGate speech work also shows that different implanted regions contribute differently to a decoder.
ideas.interpretation: Working hypothesis: the best expansion route is task dependent. Local density may reveal richer signal structure; wider coverage may capture information missing from the original region.
ideas.test: Retrain decoders on equal-sized subsets: dense local contacts, sparse wide coverage, and a spatially balanced control. Use repeated subsets, matched training data, and held-out days. Report geometry and signal quality.
ideas.revision: Proposed comparison, not a demonstrated preference for either architecture.

history.change: Proposed comparison, not a demonstrated preference for either architecture.

ideas.title: Count what stays useful
ideas.question: What if electrode count rises faster than stable neural access?
ideas.summary: Place a dated usable-channel count beside every nominal count. Long-term retention and the decoder’s actual inputs deserve their own history.
ideas.observation: A physical contact, a recording connection, a concurrent channel, and a decoder input are not interchangeable. In one 2023 speech study, 256 implanted electrodes supplied 128 electrodes used by the principal decoder.
ideas.interpretation: Working hypothesis: a count measured at a fixed implant age will explain practical progress better than the largest number fabricated. Usability still needs a predeclared quality criterion.
ideas.test: Record implanted, connected, concurrently acquired, quality-passing, and decoder-used counts at fixed follow-up intervals. Keep single-unit identity, task accuracy, latency, and independent-use duration separate.
ideas.revision: Proposed measurement framework. No unreported retention fractions are estimated.

history.change: Proposed measurement framework. No unreported retention fractions are estimated.

ideas.title: More sites—or more readout?
ideas.question: When is selecting good sites more valuable than recording all of them?
ideas.summary: A large array can contain far more sites than the electronics read simultaneously. More silicon contacts do not automatically mean more concurrent data.
ideas.observation: BISC has 65,536 selectable sites and up to 1,024 concurrent channels at 8.475 kS/s; its alternative mode records 256 at 33.9 kS/s.
ideas.interpretation: Working hypothesis: site selection can increase useful access within a fixed channel budget. Some tasks may instead require broader simultaneous sampling; switching among sites is not an equivalent measurement.
ideas.test: Compare fixed and training-selected subsets at the same channel and sampling budgets, then evaluate on held-out sessions. Report raw data rate, wireless power, selection overhead, and task performance.
ideas.revision: The calculator is arithmetic for hypothetical acquisition settings, not a device power model or an information-rate estimate.

history.change: The calculator is arithmetic for hypothetical acquisition settings, not a device power model or an information-rate estimate.

ideas.title: Can a fly circuit learn a new objective?
ideas.question: What would show that feedback improves a connectome-based model on an unfamiliar task?
ideas.summary: Use the fly Bitcoin demo as a starting question about simulated reward, model plasticity and fair evaluation.
ideas.observation: Alex Wormuth describes a fly-brain Bitcoin experiment. The linked Stonkfly repository implements a computational model using a MaleCNS graph, task inputs, a fixed buy/sell/hold readout and modeled dopamine feedback. The repository says profitable learning has not been demonstrated.
ideas.interpretation: A new task can probe how a biological wiring scaffold interacts with a designed input mapping, output rule and plasticity rule. Improvement could come from any of these layers; the wiring alone does not identify the cause.
ideas.test: Use recorded inputs and simulated money. Freeze a held-out time period before tuning. Compare the intact model with disabled reward, shuffled reward, disabled plasticity and a simple fixed or randomized readout under the same transaction-cost assumptions. Repeat across seeds and inspect whether the proposed synapses change as predicted.
ideas.revision: Evidence for task learning would strengthen if reward-dependent improvement persists on unseen data and disappears under mechanism-specific controls. If a simple controller or shuffled circuit performs similarly, the circuit-specific interpretation should be revised.

ideas.title: Does a bigger brain map make a better model?
ideas.question: When does additional anatomical detail improve prediction rather than only increase model size?
ideas.summary: Connect neuron and synapse counting to model fidelity, dataset coverage and held-out validation.
ideas.observation: FlyWire, the male-fly CNS map and MICrONS provide different anatomical and functional datasets. Computational models add dynamics, parameters and task interfaces to these resources. Neurons, anatomical synapses and aggregated weighted edges are different counting units.
ideas.interpretation: Anatomical detail is a useful constraint, but its value depends on the question. A smaller circuit with relevant physiological measurements may answer a defined task better than a larger graph with uncertain dynamics. This is a research hypothesis, not a universal rule.
ideas.test: Compare nested or deliberately simplified models using the same dataset, input conditions and held-out target. Change one source of detail at a time: wiring, cell types, weights, dynamics or plasticity. Report predictive gain, parameter sensitivity and computational cost separately.
ideas.revision: A scaling claim becomes stronger if extra measured detail consistently improves unseen predictions across suitable tasks or specimens. If the effect vanishes after controlling for controller training or parameter count, model size alone is an inadequate explanation.

companies.name: Neuralink
companies.headline: Scale the whole implantation process
companies.context: N1 nominal specification · human implant architecture
companies.evidence: The 2019 wired rat platform used up to 96 threads × 32 contacts. N1 specifies 64 × 16. These are different research and clinical configurations.
companies.thought: More contacts on an existing thread and more inserted threads can both raise the total. The latter also changes anatomical coverage and placement workload.
companies.bottleneck: Investigate insertion throughput, placement yield, wireless data/power, and signal retention together. This is our engineering interpretation, not a ranking of the company’s current bottlenecks.
companies.question: At the same contact count, do more threads improve held-out decoding enough to justify the additional insertions?

companies.name: Blackrock / BrainGate
companies.headline: Ask where the next array belongs
companies.context: One 2023 speech study · not a product-wide yield
companies.evidence: That participant had four 64-contact arrays. The main speech decoder used two premotor arrays; the other regions were weakly informative for this task.
companies.thought: Replication increases contacts without shrinking each array. Placement decides whether those extra contacts carry useful task information.
companies.bottleneck: Coverage, connected channels, and quality must be measured separately. More implanted contacts cannot be assumed to produce the same number of useful inputs.
companies.question: Would an equal-sized decoder benefit more from adjacent arrays or from sampling another relevant region?

companies.name: Precision Neuroscience
companies.headline: Separate wider coverage from tighter spacing
companies.evidence: Four arrays expanded surface coverage. The 2025 design’s nominal 1,024 sites include 977 recording-sized contacts, 42 stimulation-optimized contacts, and five references.
companies.thought: A surface platform has two growth directions: tile more cortex or decrease contact spacing. Their value may differ by task and signal band.
companies.bottleneck: Determine how much neighboring signals overlap and what extra regions contribute. Layer 7-T clearance is for a passive array used for less than 30 days; it does not establish a chronic wireless BCI.
companies.question: With contact count fixed, does a larger, more sparsely sampled area outperform a smaller dense patch?

companies.name: Paradromics
companies.headline: Find the marginal value of another contact
companies.context: Connexus specification · participant-specific electrode count not established
companies.evidence: The company’s electrode-dropping analysis used 420 contacts. Its underlying SONIC benchmark studied sound decoding in sheep; the first chronic human trial implant was announced in June 2026.
companies.thought: Denser local sampling and adding another module are both hypotheses worth testing. An improving subsampling curve does not prove the performance of a denser future device.
companies.bottleneck: Measure local redundancy, long-term retention, and transfer from animal sensory benchmarks to human intended communication. The nominal 421 / analyzed 420 difference is not explained here.
companies.question: Do added nearby contacts help as much as a spatially separated group, and does that pattern transfer to human speech?

companies.name: Synchron
companies.headline: Track useful control beside electrode count
companies.evidence: The Stentrode study recorded through a brain blood vessel. It evaluated switch actions, including eye-tracking-assisted interaction and a BCI-only scanning task.
companies.thought: Reliable selection, less calibration, and independent use can improve without a larger headline count. The cited study establishes no count-expansion roadmap.
companies.bottleneck: Vascular placement and overlapping signals may shape the value of more contacts. That remains a measurement question, not a conclusion drawn from the small count.
companies.question: How does neural-only accuracy and selection time change as usable contacts are added, with assistance reported separately?

companies.name: BISC · research platform
companies.headline: Use the sites already available
companies.context: Academic surface device · pig and nonhuman-primate evidence
companies.evidence: A selectable subset is recorded concurrently: 1,024 channels at 8.475 kS/s or 256 at 33.9 kS/s. The full array is not read out at once.
companies.thought: Fabricating more potential sensing locations and widening readout are distinct routes. Selecting good locations may help within a fixed electronic budget.
companies.bottleneck: Test selection quality, temporal coverage, wireless resources, and the cost of switching. More selectable sites do not guarantee more task information.
companies.question: Does a training-selected subset outperform a fixed subset at the same channel budget on unseen sessions?
